criteria.criterion: The verify step reads .vloop/tmp/verify.json as verify/v2 only, after a session that exited 0 and also after one that timed out, exited non-zero or left no record; a session that failed to start leaves nothing to read, as at the base. Accepting a verify/v1 report from a session is a violation.
criteria.evidence: internal/driver/iterate.go verifySession reads verify/v2 after failedRun too; verify_v2_test.go TestVerifySessionRejectsV1

criteria.criterion: A valid report is kept as `<run dir>reports/verify.json` (masked, trailing newline) and the driver prints on stdout exactly one of the four lines
criteria.evidence: iterate.go prints the four forms per the contract; run_verify_test.go and verify_v2_test.go assert them

criteria.criterion: When `complete` is false and the session exited 0, the driver then warns on the warning stream `vloop: the verify session stopped before its last pass — verify the rest by hand; see <run dir>reports/verify.json`. After a session that timed out, exited non-zero or left no record, the line is followed by the base's `vloop: the verify session failed to run — verify by hand; see <run dir>run.log` and not by the stopped-early warning.
criteria.evidence: iterate.go failedRun/else-if branch matches; tested for exit non-zero and no record (timed out untested, see findings)

criteria.criterion: A report that does not validate as verify/v2 (a verify/v1 report included) is kept by no one: after a session that exited 0 the driver prints the base's `vloop: the verify session left no valid .vloop/tmp/verify.json — verify by hand`; after a failed session only the base's failed-to-run warning.
criteria.evidence: iterate.go: !ok branch warns failedWarn only when failedRun; no test covers the invalid-report-after-failed-session half

criteria.criterion: Neither `complete` nor `not_run` changes the run's ending, its exit code or any task.
criteria.evidence: verifySession returns nil; TestRunVerifyNotRunAndIncomplete asserts exit 0 and status complete

criteria.criterion: A bare `vloop brief close` on a kept verify/v2 report prints the header `verify of <run id>/<stamp>: ` followed by `no findings` or `<N> finding(s)`, then `; <M> example line(s) not run` when not_run is not empty; the findings as at the base; one line `  not run: <line> — <reason>` per entry; and `  the session stopped before its last pass` when complete is false. A kept verify/v1 report prints exactly the base's lines.
criteria.evidence: internal/cli/close.go printVerifyReport; TestCloseVerifyBlockV2 cases; the old v1 TestCloseVerifyBlock kept

criteria.criterion: The base's stub verify reports in cmd/vloop/run_verify_test.go, cmd/vloop/run_iterate_test.go and cmd/vloop/b16_e2e_test.go become verify/v2 and nothing else in those tests weakens; internal/cli/close_test.go keeps its verify/v1 reports and gains verify/v2 siblings; the work session names the contract item in its notes.
criteria.evidence: diff changes only the schema strings in the three cmd/vloop stubs; close_test.go only adds a test

criteria.criterion: Committed tests run by the go check cover every worked-example line and planted failure: in cmd/vloop/run_verify_test.go for the run lines, in internal/cli/close_test.go for the close lines, and in internal/driver/ with a stub runner whose result says the session timed out and one that left no record (the same two lines, the report kept). A case of the worked example with no test behind it fails this criterion.
criteria.evidence: internal/driver/verify_v2_test.go covers exit non-zero and no record, but no case has a runner result with TimedOut set; the criterion names the timed-out case explicitly. Also no test for an invalid report after a failed session (only the failed-to-run warning).

findings.summary: No driver test uses a stub runner whose result says the session timed out; the timed-out case named by the acceptance criterion has no test behind it
No test covers an invalid or verify/v1 report after a failed session (only the failed-to-run warning must appear)

notes: Implementation in iterate.go and close.go looks correct against the contract; only the test coverage the criterion demands is missing.
